title: On-call Incident Response Playbook - Processes, Runbooks & Comms (2026)
author: Priya Kapoor
body:
Summary
-------
This document defines Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response process, canonical runbooks for common failure modes, postmortem expectations, rotation and game day guidance, and standardized customer / status-page communication templates. The goal is a predictable, measurable response that minimizes customer impact and accelerates remediation and learning.

Scope and ownership
-------------------
- Scope: All production-facing Redwood Inference services (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, Private control-plane integrations).
- Owners: Eng SRE (primary process owner), Service owners (runtime, routing, billing), Customer Success (customer comms), Security (for incidents involving data/security).
- PagerDuty: primary incident routing for on-call alerts. See Contacts section for escalation bindings.

Incident severity and SLO triggers
----------------------------------
We use a 4-level severity model with clear thresholds and escalation rules: 
1) Sev 1 - Production-wide outage / data-loss / security incident: Immediate page to P0 PD escalation; target ack < 5 minutes. Examples: hosted API unavailable for >10% customers, data exfiltration, production DB corruption.
2) Sev 2 - Major user impact or major degradation: P1 escalation; target ack < 10 minutes. Examples: sustained p95/p99 latency spikes degrading customer SLAs, large-scale errors >5% request error rate.
3) Sev 3 - Partial impact or internal degradation: PagerDuty notification to primary on-call; ack < 30 minutes. Examples: single-region degradation, degraded background jobs.
4) Sev 4 - Minor / non-customer facing issues: Tickets and async triage. Examples: non-urgent alerts, low-severity config drift.

Key SLOs (example baselines)
- API availability (hosted): 99.95% monthly.
- Generation p95 latency (typical routes): < 300ms. p99 latency < 800ms.
- Embeddings throughput: target 95th percentile within capacity profile.
These SLOs are used to decide severity and urgency.

Incident lifecycle (high level)
-------------------------------
1) Detection: monitoring, user reports, or external telemetry triggers an alert.
2) Triage & classify: on-call acknowledges, determines severity, assigns incident lead.
3) Mitigation: apply runbook steps or emergency mitigations (traffic cut, fallback model, scale up).
4) Communication: internal (Slack #incident), external (status page / customer comms).
5) Recovery: services restored to acceptable SLOs.
6) Postmortem: write RCA, action items, rollout improvements and track closures.

Roles and responsibilities
- Primary on-call (SRE): initial triage, mitigation actions from runbooks, internal comms.
- Secondary (service owner): deep diagnostics, longer-term fixes, code-rollouts.
- Incident lead: coordinate cross-team work, postmortem owner. For Sev1/2 the incident lead should be assigned within 15 minutes.
- Communications lead (Customer Success / Eng SRE): prepares external statements and status updates.
- Security lead: engaged immediately for incidents involving PII or data exfiltration.

Escalation matrix
- PagerDuty -> Primary on-call (0-10m) -> Secondary escalation (10-20m) -> Eng SRE director (20-30m) -> Exec on-call (30m+ for Sev1).
- Slack channel: #incident-<id> created automatically for Sev2/Sev1 via PD integration.

Canonical runbooks (high level)
-------------------------------
Each runbook below includes: objective, symptoms, immediate mitigations, diagnostics, remediation steps, and rollback.

Runbook: API high error rate (5xx)
Objective: Reduce customer-facing errors and restore API success rate to baseline.
Symptoms:
- Error rate > 5% sustained for 5+ minutes across core generation endpoints.
- PagerDuty alarm: api-5xx-rate-high.
Immediate mitigations (first 10 minutes):
1) Acknowledge PD alert and post in #incident-<id>.
2) Check global dashboard: Grafana -> "API Errors Overview".
3) Run quick traffic triage: 
   - Check ingress LB health: `curl -s https://ingress.health/api/health`
   - Check service replicas: `kubectl get pods -n runtime -l app=api --no-headers`
4) If errors correlate to a single region or node pool, remove traffic or scale up that pool (see commands below).
Diagnostics:
- `kubectl logs -n runtime deployment/api --since=10m | grep ERROR | tail -n 200`
- Check model-serving runtime metrics: model-kv-cache-hits, token-generation-errors, gpu-memory-pressure.
Remediation steps (ordered):
1) If deployment pods crashing: restart pods: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/api -n runtime` and monitor pod events: `kubectl describe pod <pod>`
2) If resource pressure (GPU memory/CPU): scale nodepool or reduce batch sizes via feature-flag: `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://admin.internal/api/feature-flags/runtime.reduce_batching=true`
3) If model variant causing errors: switch traffic to fallback model variant using the routing console: set route -> model_variant = "stable-v1" (see Ops Console runbook).
4) As a last resort, enable degraded-mode: respond with cached completions or slow-path fallback that preserves availability.
Rollback: revert routing or feature-flag changes once metrics stabilize for 15 minutes.

Runbook: High tail latency (p99)
Objective: Restore tail latency to baseline (p99 within SLO).
Symptoms: p99 latency > 800ms for 10+ minutes.
Immediate mitigations:
- Post to #incident-<id> and tag @runtime-oncall.
- Check batching and queueing metrics: batch_size_avg, request_queue_length.
Quick actions:
1) Inspect autoscaling groups and increase concurrency limits if safe.
2) Temporarily reduce batching window configuration: `kubectl edit configmap runtime-config -n runtime` and set `batch_window_ms` from 50 -> 20.
3) If KV cache misses are high, warm caches for hot prefixes or roll back recent model re-quantization.
Diagnostics commands:
- `curl -s http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))`
- Check GPU utilization: `nvidia-smi` on affected nodes (via bastion).

Runbook: Model OOM / GPU memory pressure
Immediate mitigation:
- Evict non-critical pods from affected GPU nodes: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then scale up replacement nodes.
- Switch affected traffic to model-quantized variant with lower memory footprint.

Postmortem template (required for all Sev1/Sev2 and recommended for recurring Sev3)
-----------------------------------------------------
Include these sections in the postmortem document: 
1) Title and incident id
2) Severity and timeline (UTC) with key events (detection, mitigation, recovery)
3) Impact summary (customers affected, downtime/latency windows, data loss if any)
4) Root cause analysis (why), with evidence and diagrams as needed
5) Corrective actions (short-term mitigations) and long-term fixes (owners + ETA)
6) Follow-ups (postmortem review date, verification steps, closure criteria)
7) Lessons learned and checklist updates (runbooks, monitoring, alerts)
8) Links: dashboards, logs, PD incident, PRs, KB articles
Example required fields:
- Postmortem owner: <name>
- Target to publish: within 72 hours for Sev1/2, 7 days for Sev3
- Action item tracking: link to Jira Epic or internal tracker

On-call rotations and responsibilities
------------------------------------
- Rotation model: weekly primary on-call (Mon-Fri Fri-night handover) with a dedicated weekly secondary.
- Handover protocol: primary creates summary message on Friday handover in #oncall-handover with outstanding incidents, ongoing mitigations, and blocked items.
- Timezone coverage: Primary on-call is assigned regionally; but for Sev1 incidents we escalate globally.
- Backup: each on-call must have a designated backup (vacation coverage) and update the PD schedule at least 48 hours in advance.
- Overtime policy: see People Ops handbook; all on-call work tracked for compensation/time-off adjustments.

Game days (training)
--------------------
Purpose: Validate runbooks, alerting, and team coordination under realistic conditions.
Cadence: Quarterly for SRE + product-service owners.
Sample game day plan:
1) Objective: Validate API error rate runbook and status communications.
2) Inject: Simulated service returning 502s for 10 minutes in a canary region.
3) Observe: Time-to-detect, time-to-ack, time-to-mitigate, and accuracy of status updates.
4) Debrief: Runbook gaps, monitoring gaps, and action items assigned.

Status page and customer comms templates
---------------------------------------
Status page guidance:
- Update cadence: initial update within 15 minutes for Sev1/Sev2, then every 30 minutes until recovery, then final cleared update with root-cause summary.
- Templates must be clear about scope, impact, ETA, and mitigations in place.

Status page template (short):
- Title: Service Degradation - API Errors (Partial/Complete)
- Summary: We are experiencing elevated 5xx error rates for the hosted API affecting a subset of customers. Our team is investigating.
- Impact: Customers in region(s): us-west-2 may see failed requests or degraded performance.
- ETA: Next update in 30 minutes.
- Mitigation: Traffic is being routed to fallback model variants; additional capacity being provisioned.
- Updates: [timestamped list of updates]

Customer email / support message (example):
Subject: Incident: Redwood API degraded (we're working on it)
Body:
Hello {CustomerName},

We are investigating an incident affecting generation requests in {region}. Some requests are returning failures or experiencing high latency. Our engineering team has identified the cause as {short cause} and is applying mitigations.

What we are doing:
- Routing traffic to fallback variants and adding capacity to affected pools.
- Monitoring customer-specific usage and applying rate limits where needed to protect stability.

What you can expect:
- Next update by {time}
- We will follow up with a full postmortem if you were affected.

Contact: support@redwood.inference (for customer-specific escalation)

Internal status update template (Slack):
- [INC-<id>] Sev<level> | Short title
- Impact: summary (services, regions, customers)
- Owner: <name> (Primary/Secondary)
- Mitigation in flight: bullet list
- Next update: in 15/30 minutes

Communication rules
- Keep public status updates factual and free of internal debugging details.
- Route customer-specific sensitive info through Customer Success / Account teams.
- Security incidents must include a brief "data-security" placeholder on the public status if customers may be affected, and Security will coordinate external legal notices.

Post-incident follow-up and verification
--------------------------------------
- Verification: owners must verify fixes in production for at least 72 hours before closing the incident.
- Action items: must include owner, due date, and verification steps. Track in Jira and link from postmortem.
- Runbook updates: any changes discovered during incident response must be checked into the runbook library within 5 business days.

Appendix: contacts and links
----------------------------
- PagerDuty: Redwood PD (primary): escalation policy "prod-severity".
- Slack channels: #incidents, #oncall-handover, #sre-ops.
- Dashboards: Grafana -> API Errors Overview, Runtime Health, Model Serving KPIs.
- Runbook repository: confluence: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response (canonical folder).
- Postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template-2025

--------------
